id: GB-02 repo mode with Git for Windows' drive-form paths
note: Sitting 4, P1. Git for Windows prints the toplevel and the git dirs in drive form (C:/...). git::where kept them as printed, repomode joined C:/... to the cwd, no repo_roots entry matched and repo mode was never accepted; the hint then named a C:/... folder that the settings refused. The paths are now read in this platform's form where they enter (util::posix_form: git::where, git::measure, skills gitfacts, a .git file's gitdir lines), and a repo_roots entry in drive form is read the same way. Seams: STORE_TEST_OS=msys, STORE_TEST_CYGDRIVE (C: reads as $TMP/cyg/c), and a git first on PATH that prints $TMP/cyg/c/... as C:/....

setup.script:
out=$(PATH=${PATH#*:} git "$@"); rc=$?
[ -n "$out" ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed 's#/[^ ]*/cyg/c/#C:/#g'
exit $rc

steps.name: the git first on PATH prints the toplevel and the common dir in drive form
a repository listed in repo_roots: accepted
a worktree git made for it: accepted through its main checkout
a repository listed in repo_roots in drive form (C:\w\repo2): accepted
a repository not listed: the accept hint names it in the form the settings read

stdout_has: ^  this repository asks for repo mode; to accept it, add \S+/cyg/c/w/repo3 to repo_roots in /config

steps.name: the settings writer reads a drive-form repo_roots entry as an absolute path (it still never writes the consent key)
macOS or Linux: a drive-form entry is still not an absolute path

stdout_has: ^  repo_roots: the value given: entry 1: not an absolute path$

steps.name: a linked worktree whose .git file and admin gitdir name each other in drive form
macOS or Linux: drive-form gitdir lines name no linked worktree
